title: Emotion in Reinforcement Learning Agents and Robots: A Survey
extended_summary:
This paper surveys computational models of emotion in reinforcement learning (RL) agents and robots. Its central question is how emotion has been represented in AI systems that learn from reward, and how those emotion models relate to RL mechanisms such as motivation, value functions, temporal-difference error, and action selection. The survey is intended to bridge work across machine learning, affective modeling, and human-robot interaction.

The paper is not an empirical study of learners in classrooms; instead, it reviews 52 prior papers and organizes them into a taxonomy of emotion elicitation, emotion type, and emotion function. It distinguishes four main emotion-elicitation routes: homeostasis/extrinsic motivation, appraisal/intrinsic motivation, value/reward-based elicitation, and hard-wired sensory links. It also reviews categorical and dimensional emotion models and shows how emotions can modify reward, state, meta-learning, action selection, or remain epiphenomenal.

The context is AI agents and robots, including learning architectures that may use internal drives, appraisal-like features, or reward-based signals to produce emotion-like states. The authors conclude that emotions in RL are useful for improving learning efficiency, increasing transparency and social signaling, and providing testbeds for emotion theories. They also note that many existing papers are difficult to replicate because the mapping from elicitation method to emotion type is often underspecified.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative survey and taxonomy paper, not an empirical study of educational intervention effects. It does not report a study design, sample, or causal identification strategy relevant to K-12 outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct educational outcome impact; it is foundational background on affective RL and emotion modeling in agents, with no measured effect on learners or schools.

interventions.use_case: Survey of computational emotion models in reinforcement learning agents and robots, focusing on how emotion is elicited, represented, and used within the agent learning loop.
